tip.title: Dynamic Programming Mastery
tip.advice: Define clear subproblems and states first. Write down base cases and transition equations on paper before coding. Focus on identifying overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure.

tip.title: Graph Algorithms Strategy
tip.advice: Check graph constraints carefully: directed vs undirected, weighted, cyclic, or trees. Master BFS/DFS for traversals, Dijkstra for non-negative shortest paths, and DSU for connected components.

tip.title: Data Structures Precision
tip.advice: Choose the simplest structure that supports your operations within the time limit. Practice Segment Trees, Fenwick Trees (BIT), and Monotonic Stacks until they feel second nature.

tip.title: Mathematical Insight
tip.advice: Look for symmetries, modular arithmetic properties, prime factorizations, and combinatorics patterns. Calculate small cases by hand to spot sequences and invariant relationships.

tip.title: Greedy Choice Verification
tip.advice: Greedy algorithms require rigorous proof: verify if local choices never rule out global optima. Sort by end-time, ratio, or natural order, and test edge cases like ties and reversals.

tip.title: String Processing Techniques
tip.advice: Learn polynomial rolling hash with double modulo for substring comparisons. Use Trie for prefix searches and KMP or Z-algorithm for linear pattern matching.

tip.title: Tree Traversal & Rerooting
tip.advice: Exploit tree hierarchy with tree DP, LCA (binary lifting), and Euler tour flattening to convert subtree queries into array range queries.

tip.title: Binary Search on Answer
tip.advice: When the answer space is monotonic (if X is possible, any Y >= X is also possible), frame the problem as a check(mid) boolean predicate. Be vigilant with mid calculation to prevent infinite loops.

tip.title: Constructive Thinking
tip.advice: Work backwards from the target state or build inductive patterns (n=1, n=2, n=3). Avoid overcomplicating: constructive problems usually have an elegant, symmetric invariant.

tip.title: Two Pointers & Sliding Window
tip.advice: Maintain invariant bounds where the right pointer expands and the left pointer shrinks the window once conditions violate. Great for contiguous subsegments and subarray sums.
